gloss: misfortune; bad luck; calamity; unlucky age

definitions.explanation: Ill fortune or disaster that befalls someone, often thought to have a supernatural or karmic cause.
Specific ages in Japanese superstition considered prone to misfortune (yakudoshi). Traditionally 25, 42, and 61 for men; 19, 33, and 37 for women.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}で{厄|やく}を{落|お}としてもらった。
examples.english: I had my misfortune cleansed at a shrine.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}は{厄|やく}が{多|おお}い{年|とし}だった。
examples.english: This year was a year full of misfortune.

examples.japanese: {来年|らいねん}{厄|やく}に{当|あ}たる。
examples.english: Next year falls on an unlucky age.

examples.japanese: {厄|やく}の{年|とし}には{大|おお}きな{決断|けつだん}を{避|さ}けたほうがいい。
examples.english: It's better to avoid major decisions during your unlucky year.

examples.japanese: {厄|やく}が{明|あ}けたので、やっと{安心|あんしん}した。
examples.english: My unlucky period is over, so I'm finally relieved.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{厄|やく}を{払|はら}う (ward off misfortune)
・{厄|やく}を{落|お}とす (cleanse misfortune)
・{厄|やく}に{当|あ}たる (fall on an unlucky age)
・{厄|やく}が{明|あ}ける (unlucky period ends)
・{厄年|やくどし} (unlucky year/age)

USAGE NOTES:
The concept of {厄年|やくどし} (unlucky ages) is deeply rooted in Japanese folk belief. The most feared unlucky ages are {大厄|たいやく}: 42 for men and 33 for women, both of which have wordplay associations with death ({四十二|しじゅうに} sounds like {死|し}に, and {三十三|さんじゅうさん} like {散々|さんざん}). Many people visit shrines for {厄払|やくはら}い (misfortune-cleansing rituals) at these ages.
